answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to post a refundable bond, then slash that bond if the identity is caught double-claiming rewards or coordinating duplicate work. Reputation and voting weight grow only through tasks verified by independent peers, so creating a thousand accounts does not create a thousand trusted voices. An attacker must lock up real capital in copper-backed collateral and risk losing it; spreading accounts across an ocean of nodes or along a network ridge does not evade the shared bond rule.
